purpose: Interventions tried against the Tier 2 generalisation failure, and what each measured. Surfaced by GET /ai/detection/status so the console can show why the model is disabled rather than only that it is.
task: binary GPS Spoofing vs Normal, leave-one-flight-out, pooled over held-out rows

trivial_baselines.note: Reference points that require no model at all. A detector that does not clear these is not adding information.

interventions.name: Deployable feature set, unnormalised
interventions.description: altitude, yaw and seven rate-of-change features. The registered v2 model.
interventions.reason: Flags 86% of normal rows. Far below the always-say-attack baseline.

interventions.name: Drop high-ICC flight-identity features
interventions.description: diagnostics/15 found battery (ICC 0.77), link_data_rate (0.67), pitch (0.65) and speed (0.54) carry flight identity. diagnostics/16 removes them.
interventions.reason: No measurable effect on cross-flight generalisation. The confounds were real but removing them did not recover signal, which indicates the shortcut is not carried by those four features alone.

interventions.name: Rates of change only, dropping absolute altitude and yaw
interventions.description: SWARMGUARD_FEATURE_SET=deltas. Tests whether two weakly-flight-specific absolute features jointly encode identity.
interventions.reason: F1 improves 68% but the false-positive rate gets worse, 0.862 to 0.887. The gain is recall bought with more false alarms, not better discrimination. Still below the trivial baseline.

interventions.name: Per-flight normalisation against an early-window baseline
interventions.description: Each feature z-scored against the first K rows of its own flight, so the model sees deviation from that aircraft's own behaviour rather than absolute values that encode which flight it is.
interventions.reason: The largest single improvement measured: F1 0.085 to 0.282 and the false-positive rate roughly halved. It is still rejected for three reasons. It does not clear the always-say-attack baseline of 0.574 at any window size. The result swings non-monotonically from 0.199 to 0.523 on an arbitrary window parameter, a 2.6x spread with no trend, which is the signature of an unstable estimate over 9 folds rather than a real effect. And it cannot be deployed as measured: is_attack is constant across every flight in this dataset, so the baseline window is computed from attacked data, whereas a live aircraft would baseline against a genuinely clean window after arming.

interventions.name: Per-flight normalisation over the whole flight (control, not deployable)
interventions.description: Normalises each flight by statistics taken across all of its rows, including the held-out ones. Included only as an upper bound.
interventions.reason: Precision exactly 1.000 and a false-positive rate of exactly 0.000 across 23,578 normal rows is the signature of leakage, not accuracy. The whole-flight standard deviation is itself a flight-level quantity, and attack_type is 1:1 with flight_id, so the normalisation constant carries the label. Reported to show where the ceiling comes from, never as a candidate.

root_cause.finding: The failure is structural in the dataset, not a modelling deficiency.
evidence: attack_type is 1:1 with flight_id: every flight is entirely one class, so in training 'predict the attack' and 'predict which flight' are the same task.

is_attack is constant within all 16 flights. Labels are flight-level, not sample-level, so quiescent moments of a spoofing flight are still labelled attack and recall is measured against rows that may carry no attack signal.
Nine flights means nine LOFO folds, four positive and five negative. The variance of any estimate over that is large enough to swamp the effects being measured.
root_cause.implication: No feature engineering can separate attack behaviour from flight identity while the two are the same variable. This needs data with sample-level labels and attacks that begin partway through a flight.

decision.decided_on: the leave-one-flight-out result against a trivial baseline, not on relative improvement
decision.statement: Per-flight normalisation improved the headline metric by more than 3x and is still not a detector. Tier 2 remains disabled and the kinematic guard remains authoritative.
